items.question: What was net revenue by region last calendar quarter vs the one before?

items.question: Compare net revenue in 2025 with 2024

  ROUND(

     MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN net_revenue END))
    / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN net_revenue END), 0),
    4
  ) AS pct_change
FROM yearly;

items.question: At which local hour of the day did APAC customers place the most orders in 2025?
items.sql:

  SELECT
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE r.timezone)::int AS local_hour

  WHERE o.region_code = 'APAC'
    AND o.ordered_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.ordered_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

  local_hour,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM apac_orders
GROUP BY local_hour
ORDER BY order_count DESC, local_hour

items.question: Which EU country drove the drop from the second to the third calendar quarter?
items.sql:
WITH q2 AS (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    SUM(net_revenue_usd) AS net_revenue_q2
  FROM order_revenue
  WHERE region_code = 'EU'
    AND order_date >= DATE '2026-04-01'
    AND order_date < DATE '2026-07-01'
  GROUP BY country_code
),
q3 AS (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    SUM(net_revenue_usd) AS net_revenue_q3
  FROM order_revenue
  WHERE region_code = 'EU'
    AND order_date >= DATE '2026-07-01'
    AND order_date < DATE '2026-10-01'
  GROUP BY country_code
)
SELECT
  c.code AS country_code,
  c.name AS country_name,
  ROUND(COALESCE(q2.net_revenue_q2, 0), 2) AS net_revenue_q2_2026,
  ROUND(COALESCE(q3.net_revenue_q3, 0), 2) AS net_revenue_q3_2026,
  ROUND(COALESCE(q3.net_revenue_q3, 0) - COALESCE(q2.net_revenue_q2, 0), 2) AS net_revenue_diff,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(q2.net_revenue_q2, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND((COALESCE(q3.net_revenue_q3, 0) - COALESCE(q2.net_revenue_q2, 0)) / COALESCE(q2.net_revenue_q2, 0), 4)
  END AS net_revenue_pct_change
FROM q2
FULL OUTER JOIN q3 USING (country_code)
JOIN countries c ON c.code = COALESCE(q2.country_code, q3.country_code)
ORDER BY net_revenue_diff ASC
LIMIT 1;
items.answer: Germany drove the drop from the second to the third calendar quarter of 2026. Its net revenue fell from $43,660.16 in Q2 2026 to $23,128.03 in Q3 2026, a decline of $20,532.13. This represents a percent change of –47.03%.

items.question: For every pair of orders, count how many pairs have the second order larger than the first
items.sql:
WITH ord AS (
    SELECT net_revenue_usd
    FROM order_revenue
    WHERE order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
      AND order_date < DATE '2026-10-01'
      AND net_revenue_usd IS NOT NULL
),
agg AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS n,
        SUM(cnt * (cnt - 1) / 2) AS equal_pairs
    FROM (
        SELECT net_revenue_usd, COUNT(*) AS cnt
        FROM ord
        GROUP BY net_revenue_usd
    ) g
)
SELECT (n * (n - 1) / 2 - equal_pairs) AS pairs_second_larger
FROM agg;
items.answer: The query counted ordered pairs of orders where the second order's revenue is larger than the first's, yielding 392,712,747 such pairs. This figure represents the total number of unordered pairs with distinct revenue values across all orders in the dataset. No additional calculations were performed beyond the value returned.
